title: Microsoft 365: pay-as-you-go meter for SharePoint storage above the tenant quota
summary: Hold: the controls table incorrectly says no storage-monitoring API is documented, although Microsoft documents a SharePoint storage usage report in Microsoft Graph. The rollout, opt-in default and published consumption pricing are supported, but the assurance of no new data access is not explicitly documented.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disconnecting the service is the only documented way to stop billing.
claims.quote: The only way to stop billing is to disconnect the payment method.
claims.fix: Replace the exclusivity claim with 'Disconnect the service to stop this meter; the budget does not stop billing.' The broader terms at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/microsoft-365-pay-as-you-go-terms-of-service also document cancelling or deleting the Azure subscription to stop processing and billing; do not imply that disabling a whole subscription is necessary.

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for monitoring SharePoint storage usage.
claims.quote: Get the trend of storage allocated and consumed during the reporting period. ... GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/reports/getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7')
claims.fix: Replace controls[4].api: null with the documented Graph report GET /v1.0/reports/getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7'), using this reference URL. Note that it requires Reports.Read.All and reports storage usage trends, not a live PAYGO billing balance or an exact replica of the Active sites quota bar. Alternatively narrow the row to the specific Active sites quota-bar readout and explicitly distinguish the documented usage-report API.
